article_content: A church in Tupelo, Mississippi has released striking security camera footage showing a massive tornado tearing through its playground on April 28, destroying nearly everything except a single slide. A series of tornadoes devastated several states in the Southeastern United States late last month, resulting in at least 35 deaths and millions of dollars in damages. Brad Bullock, technical director for St. Luke’s United Methodist Church, described seeing the footage to NBC News: 'It really kind of brings everything back, seeing it a week later.' The camera captured the playground just moments before the tornado hit. As winds intensified, the video shifted from color to black and white. During the tornado's peak, the playground became nearly invisible. According to Bullock, 'the building was really damaged. About 50 percent of the front of the building is gone.' After the tornado, many church members were left without power, and some lost their homes. When the storm cleared, the extent of the destruction became clear—nearly all of the playground equipment was ruined, except for a slide in the background. 'A lot of folks are displaced,' Bullock noted. 'You can’t even see the houses right now. This neighborhood had huge, beautiful oak trees that survived the 1936 tornado, and a lot of those are gone too.' Despite the devastation, Bullock remains optimistic the church will reopen: 'Our pastor went through Katrina, so he has experience in these situations. We're estimating it will take 18 months to two years to reopen. Right now, people are out assessing the damage.'

article_content: Liverpool’s current situation is dominated by discussions about Steven Gerrard’s future. Mario Balotelli, among others, must appreciate the shift in focus after a week of speculation about Gerrard’s contract, which expires next summer. Though linked to possible moves to America or Manchester City, Gerrard is expected to remain at Anfield for now. Manager Brendan Rodgers greeted Balotelli ahead of Liverpool’s crucial Champions League fixture at Real Madrid’s Bernabeu stadium. Attention has also turned to statements Gerrard made about the team improving and new signings getting better over time. Liverpool’s on-field problems are stark compared to other European heavyweights. Real Madrid have scored 54 goals this season, far surpassing Bayern Munich, Chelsea, Manchester City, Paris Saint-Germain, and Barcelona. Liverpool have scored only 19, with 11 different players on the scoresheet. Cristiano Ronaldo leads with 22 individual goals. Madrid have a 76.5% win rate, have won 13 of 17 games, and are unbeaten in their last 18 home Champions League matches. Liverpool lost influential forward Luis Suarez last summer, and new signings like Dejan Lovren, Adam Lallana, Emre Can, Lazar Markovic, and Rickie Lambert have not yet delivered consistent performances. Liverpool’s league form has suffered, losing to Newcastle after drawing with Hull City. Their last match against Madrid ended in a 3-0 defeat at Anfield. Rodgers maintains a positive outlook, viewing the away game against Madrid as an opportunity. He stressed that Liverpool came seeking a result and not expecting to lose. Despite the odds, Liverpool’s Champions League hopes remain alive if they win their last two group games, depending on other results. Real Madrid, under Carlo Ancelotti, are in excellent form. The team has won their last 11 games, scoring 24 goals in the process—17 more than Liverpool in the same period. Gareth Bale is set to return after missing the earlier fixture through injury. Rodgers acknowledges that integrating new and younger players will take time, stating that significant investment has been made to allow these players a chance to perform. Liverpool will rely on key players like Raheem Sterling and Jordan Henderson to rise to the challenge in Madrid. To compete, Liverpool must show marked improvement from their last meeting, where they lost momentum after Ronaldo’s early goal. Overall, the club faces significant challenges but holds on to some optimism and belief in their developing squad.

article_content: Mike Phelan has officially joined Norwich City as their new first-team coach. Well recognized for his previous role as assistant manager at Manchester United, Phelan’s history with Norwich runs deep. He played 194 games for the club between 1985 and 1989, captained the team, and contributed to their 1986 Second Division title win. Later, he returned as a coach in 1995, collaborating with Gary Megson and helping coach Neil Adams, who is now Norwich’s manager. Phelan was inducted into the club’s Hall of Fame in 2002. Over his playing career, Phelan appeared for Burnley (208 apps, 13 goals, 1980–85), Manchester United (148 apps, 3 goals, 1989–94), and West Brom (23 apps, 0 goals, 1994–96), and represented England once in 1989. His transfer to Manchester United from Norwich in 1989 was valued at £750,000. At Manchester United, he enjoyed various successes before joining Sir Alex Ferguson’s coaching team. Phelan’s move to Norwich is his first footballing role since leaving Manchester United in 2013. He re-joins the Norwich coaching team alongside Neil Adams and Gary Holt. Neil Adams described Phelan as the ideal replacement for Mark Robson, emphasizing his in-depth experience and strong Norwich connection. Phelan shared his enthusiasm about returning to Carrow Road, expressing his hope to help the club reach the Premier League once more.

article_content: Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, in a Sunday interview with Germany’s ARD broadcaster, accused the United States of trying to destabilize Syria through political support for opposition rebels. Assad argued that a proposed peace plan had not failed, but faced setbacks because some countries were supporting what he labeled 'terrorists.' The interview aired as the opposition’s Local Coordination Committees of Syria reported 60 more deaths in the ongoing conflict that day. That same day, U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton suggested the Assad regime was near its end, citing high-profile defections and saying, 'the sand is running out of the hourglass.' United Nations Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon also commented Sunday that the conflict in Syria had gotten much worse, with increased violence, militarization, and 'appalling' human rights abuses. Ban called for fundamental changes, saying the current situation cannot be sustained. Assad insisted that only Syrians should decide their country’s future, not outside powers, emphasizing that representation should be determined via elections. In March, former U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, acting as joint envoy for the U.N. and Arab League, arranged a six-point peace plan, which Syria’s government accepted. The plan called for ending violence, granting humanitarian access, and encouraging political dialogue. Assad described Annan's efforts as difficult but not failed, noting obstacles remain. Annan was in Damascus for discussions with Assad, according to his spokesperson. When asked about a unity government in Syria, Assad replied that such a structure already existed, referencing December’s local elections where some opposition candidates won seats. He attributed limited opposition success to voter choices. Assad claimed that U.S. political backing of opposition forces makes them complicit in Syrian civilian deaths. Further, he accused Saudi Arabia and Qatar of arming rebels, referring to foreign ministers’ public remarks but acknowledged lacking direct evidence. He also alleged Turkey is supporting weapons smuggling operations. State-run news agency SANA reported that two alleged 'terrorists' confessed to smuggling arms and fighters from Turkey, with one admitting to training from Turkish security forces. SANA added that Syrian authorities had prevented more armed groups from crossing the border, reporting casualties among the attackers. Regarding the Houla massacre, where over 100 people, many children, died in May, Assad said armed groups disguised themselves in army uniforms to incriminate the government, an alleged rebel tactic. Assad described his approach as twofold: combating terrorism and pursuing dialogue and reform. He said reforms are progressing as fast as circumstances permit, and their timeline is dependent on national conditions. The U.N. estimates the Syrian conflict, which began in March 2011, has killed over 10,000 people, while the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights cites over 16,700 deaths, most civilians. CNN noted the challenge of independently confirming these figures due to journalist access restrictions.

article_content: The Dambusters raid is remembered as one of World War II’s boldest bombing operations, and marked the first mission for 20-year-old RAF navigator Vivian Nicholson. His crew was ultimately the one that succeeded in breaching the Mohne Dam with a bouncing bomb after previous attempts by four other 617 Squadron aircraft had failed, resulting in immense relief and celebration. A 1941 training photo in Alabama shows Nicholson with an RAF colleague, while a separate image from 1943 captures a Lancaster deploying the bouncing bomb. Staying true to the stoic British manner, Nicholson penned ‘Bomb dropped. Wizard’ in his flight logbook—a comment reminiscent of popular adventure stories of the era. Flight Sergeant Nicholson wrote this line in the ‘general observations’ column as his Lancaster weaved past heavy anti-aircraft fire in the early hours of May 17, 1943. Though logbooks usually documented flight data, Nicholson’s excitement led him to insert this personal note. Piloting the aircraft ‘Johnny’ from RAF Scampton in Lincolnshire, Nicholson and his crew were among 19 Lancasters equipped with Barnes Wallis-designed bombs. With the raid’s 70th anniversary approaching, Nicholson’s log—one of five Dambuster logbooks—has been revealed to the public for the first time and is set for auction. Nicholson, who hailed from Sherburn village in County Durham and had been a joiner’s apprentice, joined the RAF in February 1941. His Lancaster was flown by Flight Lieutenant David Maltby and the mission led by Wing Commander Guy Gibson, both featured in the well-known 1954 film. The logbook records that the operation, officially named Operation Chastise, began at 9:20 pm on May 16. Entries mention severe enemy fire, forcing four evasive maneuvers, and describe how the navigation system repeatedly malfunctioned. As they neared the Mohne Dam, Nicholson documented spotting the target, arming the bomb, and dropping it at 12:49 am on May 17. In total, the crew flew 954 miles over 289¼ minutes, returning to base at 3:11 am. Only 11 out of the 19 Lancasters returned; out of 133 crew members, 53 lost their lives and three were captured. The five newly surfaced logbooks, each chronicling different aircraft during the raid, were originally estimated to fetch between £1,500 and £2,500 together, though buyers thought the group might sell for up to £10,000. JS Auctions in Banbury, Oxfordshire, has postponed the sale pending an RAF inquiry into their release and the legality of the transaction. Auctioneer Tony Cribb said the current owner’s late father had purchased the logbooks around 35 years ago during a fundraiser for the RAF Benevolent Fund. ‘The sale is postponed while the RAF determines what happened previously. We and the seller believe everything is above-board, but the RAF suspects an error occurred when the logbooks left their custody. They’re now seeking to resolve the issue,’ he explained. Included among the records is the logbook from aircraft ‘P-Peter’, which also targeted the Mohne Dam but failed to hit the mark, and the log of ‘H-Harry’, intended for the Sorpe Dam, which had to abort the mission after losing its bomb to a wave. For his actions, Flight Sergeant Nicholson was awarded the Distinguished Flying Medal. Sadly, only months after the Dambusters mission, he was killed during another raid against the Dortmund-Ems canal near Ladbergen, Germany. The Dambusters operation ultimately destroyed the Mohne and Edersee Dams, triggering devastating floods in the Ruhr valley—Germany’s industrial core—as well as villages in the Eder valley. The Sorpe Dam sustained only minor damage.

article_content: Dr. Ashley Sibery, a 39-year-old GP from Edinburgh, avoided prison after injecting his wife, Sital, with heroin to let her experience its effects. In April, following an admission to Sital about his heroin use, Sibery was confronted by his wife, who threatened to end their marriage unless he stopped. He is required to appear in court again next year for progress monitoring.

Marc Paskin, a 63-year-old millionaire real estate developer from San Diego, gained international attention after putting up a $4,000 billboard in Barrio Logan, stating: 'All I Want for Christmas is a Latina Girlfriend.' The sign quickly drew media coverage around the world and resulted in more than 15,000 responses from women across the U.S. and abroad.

Women who responded represented a range of backgrounds. Andrea, 38, a single, well-traveled woman with a master’s degree in education, said she saw nothing to lose in reaching out. Arcilia Ruiz, a 59-year-old unemployed grandmother, shared that she had never been 'swept off her feet.' Liza, age 44 and divorced, originally from Ecuador, cited her love of picnics and salsa dancing, saying she hoped to feel special. Natalie Quntero, 28, a mother and business student, expressed similar interest.

While some local residents found the billboard humorous, others thought it was inappropriate or offensive. The ad was vandalized within days, with Paskin’s email address removed first, then the entire billboard taken down by week’s end. Paskin chose not to replace it, explaining, 'Everyone has a right to find love and happiness—I just went about it in a different way.'

Paskin’s wife Marsha passed away in 2002 after 28 years of marriage. He has two children and three grandchildren. Known for his philanthropy, Paskin was featured on ABC’s ‘Secret Millionaire,’ donating over $125,000 during the show and more than $1.3 million to vision-related organizations. He expressed gratitude for the strong response and wished all a Merry Christmas and 'Feliz Navidad.'

article_content: Caroline Kennedy began her tenure as U.S. ambassador to Japan in November 2013 with initial meetings at Japan’s Foreign Ministry. Arriving in Tokyo accompanied by her husband Edwin Schlossberg, she delivered greetings from President Obama — a nod to her close connection to the White House. Japanese analysts and commentators view Kennedy’s personal relationship with Obama as a significant diplomatic asset. Her endorsement of Obama in the 2008 Democratic primary demonstrated their strong ties. At age 55, Kennedy is the first woman appointed to this ambassadorial post in Japan. Many observers consider her a potential role model for women, given her public service lineage as President John F. Kennedy’s daughter. She stated her commitment to upholding her father’s legacy and strengthening U.S.-Japan relations. While relations between Japan and the United States are generally stable, Kennedy arrives amid ongoing negotiations, including the Trans-Pacific Partnership, U.S. military base relocation in Okinawa, and defense cooperation revision. Experts have pointed out that the working relationship between Obama and Prime Minister Shinzo Abe lacks some personal warmth. Kennedy received a notably positive welcome in Tokyo, which State Department spokesperson Jen Psaki described as evidence of the strong ties between the two nations. Addressing Kennedy’s limited diplomatic background, Psaki cited her longstanding commitment to public service and expressed confidence in her new role. Commentators often group U.S. ambassadors to Japan as political figures, regional experts, or presidential confidants. Kennedy, an attorney and author, falls into the last category, like her predecessors John Roos and Tom Schieffer. As the first woman in the role, her appointment is seen as a milestone and an opportunity to deepen the partnership between the U.S. and Japan.

article_content: Blind taste tests have revealed that most lager drinkers are unable to differentiate between leading European beer brands. Nearly 140 volunteers aged between 21 and 70 participated by sampling Budvar, Heineken, and Stella Artois without knowing which was which. Each was given three samples—two from the same brand and one different—and asked to identify the unique one, with most participants finding it difficult. The research was conducted by Johan Almenberg and Anna Dreber from the Stockholm School of Economics, together with Robin Goldstein, author of 'The Beer Trials' and the forthcoming 'Blind Taste'. Goldstein stated that large brewers like Anheuser-Busch InBev and Heineken have brought a high level of consistency and quality to pale lagers, making them almost indistinguishable to most drinkers. He suggested that consumer loyalty to these brands is influenced more by marketing than by noticeable taste differences. Sean Lewis, author of 'We Make Beer', commented that this similarity shows brewers have succeeded in producing a consistent flavour profile. Despite these advancements, major beer brands have experienced stagnant or declining sales in recent years, with Germany's sales reaching a 25-year low. Conversely, craft beers are seeing increasing sales, estimated to reach £12 billion in 2014, according to the research firm Mintel.

article_content: CHISINAU, Moldova — Moldovans voted in nationwide local elections Sunday, amid claims from authorities that Russia is carrying out 'hybrid warfare' to undermine the democratic process in this European Union candidate country. Local elections in Moldova — a nation of around 2.5 million people located between Romania and Ukraine — normally receive little international attention. However, ongoing allegations of Russian interference have brought global focus to the vote. On Sunday, citizens elected nearly 900 mayors and 11,000 local councilors for four-year terms, including the mayor of the capital, Chisinau. Around 1,500 national and international observers monitored the ballot. The Central Electoral Commission reported a 41% turnout by the time polls closed at 9 p.m. — nearly identical to turnout in 2019. Just two days before the election, Prime Minister Dorin Recean announced a ban on candidates from the pro-Russian Chance Party, following a report by the national intelligence agency alleging Russian efforts to influence the vote through the party. Roughly 600 candidates were affected. "We are protecting Moldova from a well-organized network of criminals. This is about removing an organized criminal group from the elections, not a political party," Recean said at a press briefing. A 32-page report from the Intelligence and Security Service (SIS) alleged that the Chance Party received about 50 million euros ($53 million) from Russia, channeled by exiled Moldovan oligarch Ilan Shor to destabilize Moldova and 'buy' voters. Shor, now residing in Israel and sentenced in absentia to 15 years for fraud, took to Facebook to denounce the ban as an "unprecedented, illegal, raiding power grab" and posted a list of alternative endorsements. Addressing the situation, President Maia Sandu stated Sunday in Chisinau: "Elections are about democracy and compliance with the law. Those who do not follow the law, bribe voters, or use illegal funds do not meet democratic standards." If no candidate achieves at least 50% in mayoral races, a runoff will take place between the top two within two weeks. Outside a polling station in the capital, retiree Anatol Mosanu said he voted for "a better life, better roads... for tomorrow to be better than today." He added, "We all hope that in the future our children won’t leave, and we’ll be surrounded by our children and grandchildren," referencing the high emigration of Moldovans seeking better opportunities abroad. Cristian Cantir, associate professor of international relations at Oakland University, noted, "Though these elections concern local issues, they are also geopolitically important. Moldova remains very polarized, with debate hinging on pro-EU and anti-EU messaging." He also stated the SIS report contains significant evidence that Ilan Shor cooperated with Russian entities to undermine the process. In late October, authorities blocked several Russian media outlets, including Russia Today, for alleged disinformation campaigns. Days later, six television stations purportedly linked to Shor and another exiled oligarch, Vladimir Plahotniuc, had licenses suspended for allegedly promoting pro-Russian narratives and trying to influence the elections. Both Shor and Plahotniuc have been sanctioned by the US and the UK. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, non-NATO Moldova has encountered ongoing challenges, such as a severe energy crisis after Russia reduced gas supplies, rising inflation, and incidents of missile debris landing on Moldovan territory. Shor once led the pro-Russian Shor Party, declared unconstitutional by Moldova’s Constitutional Court in June after organizing months of protests against the pro-Western government, who accused the party of seeking to destabilize the country. Earlier this year, President Sandu outlined an alleged plot by Moscow to overthrow Moldova’s government and bring it under Russian control, jeopardizing its EU trajectory. Russia has denied these accusations. Moldova, a former Soviet republic, gained EU candidate status alongside Ukraine on June 23, 2022. "Russia has always sought to undermine Moldova’s democratic elections and its aspirations for European integration," Cantir observed. "We will see how effective these efforts have been." ___ Stephen McGrath contributed reporting from Sighisoara, Romania.

article_content: Google Photos is introducing an update that will allow users to create custom video slideshows based on their preferences. Instead of waiting for the app to automatically generate videos with generic titles and sometimes less-than-ideal photo selections, users will now have the ability to choose specific parameters—such as people, places, or activities—to include in their slideshows. With this update, Google Photos will scan for and select the best photos that match your chosen criteria, add music, and automatically sync everything into a video. After receiving the video, users can trim clips, rearrange them, or change the music as desired. Previously, creating these types of videos required users to manually search for and select photos. The new feature strikes a balance between manual creation and passive, automatic slideshows. Google plans to roll out this update gradually, meaning not all users will have access to it immediately. The company has not yet confirmed if the feature will be available on the web, which OS versions it will support, or which types of searches (for example, 'puppy') will work. Further details will be provided as they become available. There is also speculation about whether Apple Photos will introduce a similar feature in the future.

article_content: If you’re willing to stay up late, be patient, and put your phone away, you might catch a glimpse of the Orionid meteor shower this weekend. The shower will be visible under ideal viewing conditions. The best time to view the Orionids is from midnight to dawn, as the shower peaks between October 20 and 21, with an estimated 10 to 20 meteors per hour. Fortunately for stargazers, the moon will set around midnight, creating a completely dark sky for watching shooting stars—weather permitting, according to EarthSky. People in both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres can enjoy this event. These meteors may take some effort to spot—they are some of the fastest, traveling up to 41 miles per second towards Earth, which can make them difficult to see, according to Space.com. To maximize your chances, seek out a dark location away from light pollution. According to NASA, the Orionids are known to occasionally produce fireballs, which are especially bright meteors—a spectacular sight to witness. NASA advises looking out for these prolonged flashes of light during the meteor shower. The Orionid meteor shower is named after the Orion constellation, the apparent source of the meteors—not to be confused with the Orion Nebula. Because the constellation rises in both hemispheres, people worldwide can watch the shower, according to The Planetary Society. However, NASA and Space.com note that focusing only on Orion may cause you to miss some of the more brilliant meteors. Meteors near Orion usually have shorter tails. Scanning nearby constellations can reveal longer, more spectacular tails. So, take in the entire night sky during the shower. While not considered the most dazzling meteor shower, the Orionids remain a highlight on the calendars of many stargazers. The display is caused by debris from Halley's Comet, which passes by Earth approximately every 75 years. When Halley's Comet travels through the inner solar system, it leaves dust and rocky fragments behind. This debris triggers two yearly meteor showers: the Eta Aquarids in May and the Orionids in October. Halley's Comet is expected to return to Earth's skies in 2061.

NEW DELHI: On Monday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed his delight at the presence of diplomats from numerous countries who experienced India's rich cultural heritage during Kashi's Dev Deepavali festival. Posting on X, PM Modi stated, "Kashi is synonymous with Dev Deepavali and, this year too, the celebrations have been grand. Equally heartening is the distinguished presence of diplomats from many nations, who witnessed India's vibrant culture."

Varanasi's ghats were illuminated by millions of lamps as devotees flocked to the holy city for Dev Deepavali, also known as 'the Diwali of the Gods' or 'the festival of lights of the Gods.' The celebrations took place on Kartik Purnima, the full moon day of the Hindu month of Kartika, which this year fell on Monday, November 27—fifteen days after traditional Diwali. 

Devotees across India offered prayers at temples and ghats to mark Kartik Purnima and Dev Deepavali. At the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam, special ceremonies were held. Digha Ghat in Patna saw a large gathering of people taking a holy bath in the Ganga on Monday morning.

As darkness fell on Kartik Purnima, the ghats of Kashi appeared celestial, aglow with 2.1 million (21 lakh) earthen lamps. Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Modi participated in the Koti Deepotsavam event in Hyderabad. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the Dev Deepavali celebrations by lighting the first lamp.

The event, attended by citizens, dignitaries, ambassadors, and envoys from 70 countries, along with 150 delegates and their families, highlighted the magnificence of Kashi during the festival. Varanasi saw approximately 21 lakh lamps lit, with over 1.2 million people gathering along the crescent-shaped ghats. Notably, 100,000 of the lamps were crafted from cow dung, adding a traditional touch to the spectacular illumination.

article_content: One of the most remarkable achievements in cinema is when a film can truly transport its audience to another time and place. Ang Lee’s 'Brokeback Mountain' immerses viewers in the world of cowboys in 1960s Wyoming. Pawel Pawlikowski’s 'Cold War' takes us to the striking yet bleak landscape of 1950s Poland. Spike Lee’s 'The 25th Hour' is inseparable from post-9/11 New York. Now, John McPhail’s 'Dear David' attempts to take viewers on a journey into the psychedelically awkward core of the 2010s internet. 'Dear David' is a tepid horror film about a narcissistic blogger tormented by a ghost with an oddly wholesome anti-cyberbullying agenda. While the movie itself misses the mark, it is the epitome of meme-inspired digital culture on screen: filled with internet slang and references, it seems wholly committed to capturing the spirit of BuzzFeed-era virality, leaving viewers both bemused and fascinated. For those unfamiliar with its origins, 'Dear David' is adapted from BuzzFeed cartoonist Adam Ellis’s 2017 viral Twitter thread. In this ongoing story, Ellis recounted being haunted by a supernatural entity visiting him in dreams—starting with the tweet: 'So, my apartment is currently being haunted by the ghost of a dead child, and he's trying to kill me. (thread).' He followed up with a cartoon illustration of the spectral child, describing him as having a large, misshapen head, dented on one side. Over the subsequent months, Ellis updated followers about 'Dear David,' sharing photos and videos that, when edited for brightness, appeared to reveal the ghostly figure lurking nearby. Though clearly contrived and exhausting in retrospect, the story captivated many; digital news outlets even covered it as if it might be real. Ellis quickly amassed over a million Twitter and Instagram followers, leading to a movie adaptation. 'Dear David' is not the first film based on viral tweets—Janicza Bravo’s 'Zola' is an acclaimed example, inspired by Aziah 'Zola' King's infamous Twitter thread. Unfortunately, 'Dear David' stands as the weakest entry in tweet-based cinema, focusing on the cloying aspects of Ellis’s online presence instead of embracing the inherent absurdity of its premise. In the film, Ellis (portrayed by Augustus Prew) is depicted as a self-absorbed cartoonist who neglects his kind boyfriend and treats his friends dismissively, all while communicating in millennial internet clichés (such as the line, 'I’m relatable AF'). He attracts the attention of the malevolent spirit, 'Dear David,' after responding rudely to a negative Twitter comment—specifically, telling someone to 'DIAF,' meaning 'die in a fire.' This leads to sleep paralysis and hauntings by a ghost with the same strange, misshapen head featured in Ellis’s original cartoon (which the movie faithfully reproduces, alongside many of his tweets).

article_content: The Bihar government has issued a firm warning to newly appointed teachers, cautioning that involvement in any association or participation in protests against Education Department policies could result in strong disciplinary measures, including annulment of their provisional positions. According to a statement shared on November 11, the Education Department clarified that approximately 1.20 lakh teachers who cleared the 2023 Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) recruitment exam and received provisional appointment letters on November 2 have yet to be assigned postings or begin teaching. Despite this, authorities have discovered that some new teachers have formed associations and voiced criticism of departmental policies—actions deemed in violation of the Bihar Government Employees Conduct Rules-1976 and the Bihar School Teachers Rules 2023. The department underscored that such conduct represents significant misconduct and warned that appointments could be revoked immediately if these violations are substantiated. Officials referenced Paragraph 7 of Section 17 in the Code of Conduct for Bihar School Teachers, noting that provisionally appointed teachers are strictly prohibited from joining or creating any union or association. The department has also requested an explanation from a group office-bearer and reiterated that forming such associations is unauthorized at this stage. Despite several attempts, Education Minister Chandrashekhar was not available for comment. Raju Singh, convener of the TET Primary Teachers' Association, expressed support for the department’s stance, remarking that because the appointments are provisional, joining or forming an unregistered association is not permitted until after the probation period. He emphasized that, while everyone is entitled to express their views, this must be done in accordance with laws for government employees. The BPSC exam in August 2023 selected 1.20 lakh teachers for roles out of 1.70 lakh available posts, with appointment letters distributed in Patna and across various districts.

article_content: On Tuesday, November 7, election night had voters on edge across America, but for New York's restaurants, it was also a highly anticipated evening. The Michelin Guide held its annual awards ceremony in Tribeca, announcing the latest Michelin stars for restaurants in New York City, Chicago, and Washington, D.C. This year, twelve New York restaurants earned Michelin Star honors for the first time. Two of them, Odo and Sushi Noz, both featuring high-end Japanese cuisine, were awarded two stars each. The one-star recipients represent a variety of culinary styles. ‘The rise of Odo and Sushi Noz has been swift and impressive,’ said Gwendal Poullennec, International Director of the Michelin Guide. ‘These restaurants showcase exquisite ingredients and intricate preparation, with meticulous presentation and attentive service.’ Sushi Noz joined Odo with two Michelin stars, while many other New York City restaurants retained their prestigious accolades. Eleven Madison Park, Le Bernardin, Masa, and Per Se were all awarded three stars again. Highlights from Michelin inspectors for New York's newly starred restaurants include: Two Michelin Stars: Odo: A serene, intimate counter separates guests from the cocktail bar, creating an air of exclusivity. Under Chef Hiroki Odo, the kaiseki menu blends traditional and creative elements. Dishes feature vibrant, precise flavors, such as savory tilefish broth with yuzu and house-made soba noodles with rich salmon roe. Sushi Noz: Chef Nozomu Abe leads a refined omakase experience in a space designed as an intimate Japanese refuge. Guests enjoy specialties like sea perch with ponzu, silky eel noodles in miso soup, and jewel-like sushi, with kimono-clad staff ensuring a spirit of hospitality. One Michelin Star: Bōm: A modern Korean restaurant behind Oiji Mi, led by Chef Brian Kim and team. It features premium beef and a range of elegant, well-executed dishes with polished service. Christophe: Chef Christophe Bellanca’s cuisine balances French technique with Asian flavors, offering dishes like white asparagus in bergamot crème, blue prawns with genmaicha tuille, and braised black sea bass with shiitake chutney. Jōji: Headed by Chefs Xiao Lin, Wayne Cheng, and George Ruan, this omakase spot at One Vanderbilt earns acclaim for its quality fish and traditional approach, inspired by the chefs’ experience at Masa. Meju: Chef Hooni Kim offers a menu centered on fermented Korean ingredients, showcasing doenjang, gochujang, and more in dishes with tofu, pancakes, beef, and pork. The menu is personal, minimalist, and carefully crafted. Restaurant Yuu: Chef Yuu Shimano presents classic French cuisine viewed through Japanese omotenashi, serving approximately 20 courses with highlights like house-made toasted brioche topped with foie gras and seared wagyu. Shmoné: Chef Eyal Shani creates a daily-changing menu emphasizing fresh, grilled ingredients—even desserts like grilled figs on Chantilly cream—resulting in flavorful and focused meals. Ichimura: Renowned sushi chef Eiji Ichimura leads an edomae-style omakase experience at a 10-seat cedar counter in Tribeca, serving meticulously prepared fish sourced from Japan. Torrisi: Inside the Puck Building, Chefs Rich Torrisi, Mario Carbone, and Charlie England offer imaginative fare like escarole and endive salad, chicken stracciatella soup, and clams in grilled boule. Michelin Green Star: Dirt Candy: Chef Amanda Cohen’s restaurant focuses on a meat-free supply chain and hyper-local sourcing to minimize environmental impact. The staff reduces food waste, the kitchen is electric, and the wine program features biodynamic selections from women winemakers. Employees benefit from no-tipping, health plans, and educational support. Semma: Chef Mark Ordaz centers vegetables in the menu, complemented by grains, legumes, and dairy, with minimal meat and fish. The restaurant maintains relationships with farmers, has a rooftop garden, educates staff about sustainability, composts food waste, and uses eco-friendly furnishings and lighting.

article_content: Websites set up to raise money for Ferguson, Missouri police officer Darren Wilson have unexpectedly stopped accepting donations after collecting nearly half a million dollars. The reason for the halt is unclear. Since Wilson’s identity was publicly released on August 15, two GoFundMe pages together raised more than $433,000 to cover legal fees and other costs related to his fatal shooting of unarmed black teenager Michael Brown. By Sunday, both fundraising pages stopped accepting contributions, displaying the message: 'Donations are Complete! The organizer has stopped donations.' Wilson has been in hiding since he was named as the officer who killed Brown, who was shot at least six times on a Ferguson street. Wilson, through friends, has stated that he acted in self-defense. However, residents of the predominantly black Ferguson community are outraged, and the shooting has led to multiple days of protest. The shooting is currently under investigation by the St. Louis County Prosecuting Attorney and the Justice Department. Michael Brown’s family and supporters are demanding that Wilson be charged with murder. Meanwhile, a GoFundMe page supporting Brown’s family has raised $315,000 and continues to accept donations. According to the Los Angeles Times, a GoFundMe spokeswoman said the company is not responsible for stopping donations to the 'Support Officer Darren Wilson' and 'Support Officer Wilson' pages. Over 10,000 people contributed to the two campaigns, with the average donation around $40. Some donors gave thousands, with one person giving $10,000. The 'Support Officer Wilson' campaign, which raised $197,620, is run by Shield of Hope, a St. Louis police charity. Its directors include Timothy Zoll (Ferguson Police Department public information officer), Jeffrey Roorda (Missouri state representative), and Joseph Eagan (city councilman in Florissant near Ferguson). The 'Support Officer Darren Wilson' campaign collected $235,550 and is operated by an anonymous GoFundMe user. GoFundMe verified the identity of the page's organizer, who uses the username 'StandUp,' though no additional identifying details are provided. The organizers of the anonymous page had promised to coordinate with Shield of Hope to properly distribute the donations, but this has not yet occurred. In a related case, after George Zimmerman was arrested and charged with the fatal shooting of unarmed black teenager Trayvon Martin in 2012, more than $300,000 was raised online for his legal defense and living expenses while he was in hiding.

article_content: Set on the exclusive island of Mustique in the Grenadines, the Cotton House has become renowned as a luxury Caribbean getaway for celebrities and elite visitors. The hotel began as a sugar mill and warehouse before renowned theatre designer Oliver Messel transformed the estate into a boutique destination. Offering just 17 rooms, suites, and cottages—some with sweeping ocean views, others in lush gardens—the Cotton House is designed for maximum privacy and luxury. Larger residences come with perks like private pools and butler service, while even the entry-level options uphold an elegant standard. The Cotton House has welcomed many high-profile guests such as Cheryl Fernandez-Versini (formerly Cheryl Cole), the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge, Kate Moss, and the Beckhams. Prince William and Kate are noted for dining at the Veranda restaurant, which boasts international fare and a distinguished wine selection. More casual fare and drinks can be found at the Beach Cafe or Basil’s Bar, the island's lively local haunt and a favorite gathering spot—Kate Moss celebrated her 40th birthday here. The surrounding grounds feature tennis courts, a riding school, and a dive center. Guests get around the island by golf cart, passing immaculate beaches and private villas owned by celebrities, financiers, and fashion industry leaders. A recent renovation led by hotelier Grace Leo has kept the Cotton House’s understated Caribbean style at the forefront, highlighted by bright décor and informal elegance. Weekly drinks receptions are hosted in the spacious Great Room, and wellness is a focus at the spa—upgraded by the acclaimed British brand ila under founder Denise Leicester. For many, the Cotton House serves as an introduction to Mustique’s opulent lifestyle, with some guests eventually opting for private villa rentals or ownership—famous homeowners include Mick Jagger and Bryan Adams. Cheryl Cole also chose Mustique's Macaroni Beach for her wedding. Such exclusivity means high prices—a pizza at the Beach Cafe costs £17, with other menu items scaling upwards. Day visitors are rare unless they’re famous or influential. Vacation packages from Virgin Holidays and Hip Hotels, including seven nights’ accommodation with flights, start at £2,999 per person (prices as of 2015).

article_content: Walmart is the world's largest private employer, a distinction it holds in the United States and in many states. With over 1.5 million US employees—representing about one-tenth of the 15.5 million people working in retail—Walmart is a significant player in the industry. Statistically, a retail worker is at least three times more likely to work for Walmart than for any other single brick-and-mortar retailer. Walmart’s US workforce surpasses the combined total of the next three largest physical retailers: Target, Kroger, and Home Depot. The company operates more than 5,200 locations across all 50 states, supporting both urban and rural communities. According to company reports, a 'typical' Walmart worker is likely a woman (53% of hourly staff), identifies as white (half of the workforce), and is around 39 years old, making her an 'elder millennial.' She probably works at a Supercenter near Dallas, Texas, which has Walmart's highest store density. Texas has roughly 500 Walmart stores, 81 Sam’s Club warehouses, and employs over 175,000 workers. Her most common roles are as a stocker, who replenishes shelves, or a digital picker, who prepares online orders. These workers are often found in the store aisles, either restocking items or picking products for customers. Although she may be demographically typical, the position is demanding. An anonymous Illinois worker told Insider that sales volumes can resemble the Christmas rush every weekend. More than two-thirds of Walmart’s hourly employees work full-time, averaging at least 34 hours per week—well above the retail industry average of less than 30 hours. Employees working 30 or more hours per week are eligible for health benefits. While turnover is generally high in retail, Walmart employees typically stay for five years. CEO Doug McMillon began his Walmart career as an hourly loading dock employee, and three-quarters of managerial staff rose from hourly roles. McMillon has stated, “We’re constantly working to bring our values to life through our culture and strengthen the ladder of opportunity.” Roughly 5% of US workers hold multiple jobs, and some Walmart staff supplement their earnings with additional part-time or gig work, per the Illinois employee. Walmart does not track the number of employees with multiple jobs. Globally, Walmart employs about 600,000 people outside the US; the median worldwide wage last year was $27,136. In Texas, the average hourly wage for Walmart workers is higher at $18.12, or around $33,000 per year based on a 35-hour workweek.

article_content: Bret has been named as the second tropical storm of the 2011 Atlantic hurricane season, according to the National Weather Service. As of Sunday evening, Bret was situated about 100 miles (165 kilometers) northwest of Great Abaco Island in the Bahamas, with sustained winds at 40 mph (65 kph) and stronger gusts. The storm's winds reached out up to 35 miles (55 kilometers) from its center. Meteorologists stated the storm would likely stay nearly stationary overnight, but a slow shift toward the north-northeast is expected to start on Monday. The National Weather Service also anticipates that Bret may strengthen over the next 48 hours. A tropical storm watch has been issued for the northwest Bahamas, including Grand Bahama Island and the Abaco Islands. The storm could bring 1 to 3 inches of rain and increased surf along north- and west-facing beaches.

article_content: Christiane Amanpour is set to return to CNN International with a new weekday show, while continuing her role as global affairs anchor at ABC News, according to announcements from both networks on Tuesday. Amanpour's new program will debut on CNN International in 2012, under a unique arrangement with ABC News, CNN Worldwide President Jim Walton said in an email to staff. “Christiane Amanpour has been synonymous with international reporting and with CNN for many years,” Walton stated. “We could not be happier that, through this special collaboration with ABC News, her experience and global perspective are coming back to a nightly news broadcast for our international audience.” Since leaving CNN in 2010 to host ABC's 'This Week,' Amanpour now says she is 'thrilled and honored' to host multiple primetime specials for ABC News and to return to CNN. “I am looking forward to getting back into the field to report stories on global issues that matter greatly to the American people,” she said. “At the same time, I will once again broadcast to hundreds of millions around the world with a daily show on CNN International.” George Stephanopoulos, who previously hosted 'This Week,' will return to that program and continue as anchor of 'Good Morning America,' ABC News spokesman Jeffrey Schneider confirmed. Ben Sherwood, ABC News President, praised Amanpour's accomplishments, saying, 'Christiane has had an absolutely remarkable year at ABC News, with world-beating exclusives. We’re delighted she will bring vital global stories back to our audiences, especially in primetime.' Amanpour has spent more than 25 years reporting worldwide for CNN, most recently serving as chief international correspondent and anchor of 'Amanpour,' a 30-minute daily interview show on CNN International from September 2009 to April 2010. Her distinguished work has earned her nine News and Documentary Emmy Awards, four George Foster Peabody Awards, two George Polk Awards, three duPont-Columbia Awards, the Courage in Journalism Award, an Edward R. Murrow Award, the Television Academy Honor, and nine honorary degrees. In 2007, Queen Elizabeth II appointed Amanpour a Commander of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire for her significant and innovative contributions to journalism. Reporting by Catherine E. Shoichet for CNN.

article_content: Roads are the backbone of Nigeria's transport infrastructure and are crucial to the country's economy and development. However, recent directives mandating reinforced concrete technology have halted many ongoing road projects, as Damilola Aina reports. Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, has insisted on adopting reinforced concrete pavement for road construction, replacing the more commonly used asphalt. This decision has abruptly stopped several ongoing projects. Investigations reveal that contractors have either slowed their construction efforts or left the worksites entirely. This is due to unforeseen policy changes, insufficient funding, and the potential need to redesign roads and pavements as required by the ministry. Among the affected projects are the Abuja-Lokoja Road, Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Road, East-West Road, Enugu-Port-Harcourt Road, Benin-Warri Road, Akure-Ado-Ekiti Road, Zaria-Funtua-Sokoto-Shema Road in Kaduna, certain areas in Gusau (Zamfara), Mubi-Maiduguri and Bama-Konduga-Maiduguri Roads in Adamawa and Borno states. After his ministerial screening on August 1, 2023, Dave Umahi announced his intention to utilize reinforced concrete for road construction, claiming it would last 50 years—much longer than the typical seven-year lifespan of asphalt roads. He described concrete as maintenance-free, cost-effective, and highly durable. As an experienced engineer and former governor of Ebonyi State, Umahi criticized the short lifespans of Nigerian roads and suggested that contractors unwilling to use concrete technology would not be given government contracts. Reinforced concrete, or 'Rigid Pavement Technology,' involves combining cement, sand, coarse aggregate, and water, which is reinforced with 8–10mm bars before finishing layers are applied as needed. While cost comparisons are debated, experts agree that this method offers greater strength and durability, making it suitable for heavy-use areas like runways and tarmacs. Internationally, concrete roads constitute about 50% of major roads in some European countries and 60% in the US, Germany, and Norway. Poland leads Europe in new concrete road construction. As of 2022, Nigeria's federal road network spanned 36,000 kilometers: 24,000 km asphalt, 5,800 km gravel/earth, and 6,000 km surface-dressed. Despite the benefits, contractors and industry leaders are burdened by the decision to switch technologies. Construction firms have invested heavily in asphalt-related equipment and materials—investments now at risk. The transition to concrete necessitates expensive new machinery, such as concrete pavers costing up to 1.7 million euros (₦1.7 billion), and will increase demand for imported cement, steel, and iron, thereby raising project costs and pressuring Nigeria’s currency. Concerns have surfaced about possible contract breaches, rising material prices, and the inability to adjust contract terms. According to anonymous industry sources, contractors lack the capital for sudden equipment upgrades and struggle with delayed government payments. It is feared the ministry may also prioritize companies with existing concrete equipment, leaving others sidelined. Experts like engineer Akaninyene Ikopbo recommend a balanced approach—employing both asphalt and concrete according to project needs to ease the transition and avoid unnecessary losses. Ikopbo notes that while technology upgrades are positive, actual implementation must weigh pros, cons, and especially costs. He highlights the importance of good drainage (a weakness for asphalt roads) and points out that Nigeria’s dependence on imported materials like steel directly affects the economy. He calls for comprehensive planning and the proper maintenance of basic infrastructure. Civil engineer Ijirotimi Olarenwaju, a member of the Nigerian Society of Engineers, suggests the government consider legislation making concrete mandatory for road-building, but recognizes the need for justification, especially given regional differences (notably flood-prone southern states). He notes this approach mirrors practices in Europe and calls for legislative support, as Russia did in 2017. In summary, while the adoption of concrete roads is largely supported for its long-term benefits, stakeholders urge appropriate planning, government support for affected contractors, and a measured transition that factors in cost, expertise, and regional circumstances.

article_content: Greece will hold a snap general election in late January after parliament failed to elect a new president, raising concerns about renewed eurozone instability. Prime Minister Antonis Samaras advanced the presidential vote, aiming to prevent an early election, but his candidate, Stavros Dimas, did not secure the required majority after three rounds of voting. Greek law mandates that if no president is elected, parliament must be dissolved and elections called, creating uncertainty for financial markets and Greece’s European Union partners. This situation creates an opening for the left-wing Syriza party, which currently leads in polls with pledges to challenge Greece’s bailout terms, end austerity, and renationalize key sectors. Investors reacted by selling Greek stocks, causing the Athens stock exchange index to fall 7.3% in midday trading. Dimas, a 73-year-old former minister and European commissioner, received 160 and 168 votes in earlier rounds but needed at least 180; he again received only 168 in the final round. Syriza leader Alexis Tsipras described the vote as a 'historic day for Greek democracy.' Prime Minister Samaras announced elections will take place on January 25. Tsipras vowed to reverse austerity measures and restore wages. Recent polls show Syriza ahead of the New Democracy party by 3.3 percentage points. Greece has been making gradual economic recovery, reducing its deficit from 15% in 2009 to an expected 3% in 2014. A Syriza win could lead to the rejection of bailout terms and renewed uncertainty in the eurozone. Tsipras said European sentiment is shifting toward renegotiation. Austerity measures imposed after the 2012 bailout, which totaled €240 million, sparked public protests and riots, including violent clashes in Athens. The measures resulted in job cuts and a 22% reduction in the minimum wage. Some independent lawmakers doubt a new president could have been elected amidst political divisions. Samaras indicated there would be no further concessions to the opposition.

article_content: At a rally in Balotra, Rajasthan, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi took a jab at Prime Minister Narendra Modi by implying that Modi's presence at the World Cup final contributed to India's unexpected loss to Australia. When a member of the crowd shouted 'panauti' (meaning unlucky or bad omen), Rahul Gandhi smiled and agreed, saying, 'Yes... panauti, panauti... Our boys would have won the World Cup, but the bad omen made us lose. The media won't mention this, but people know.' His comments suggested that PM Modi's attendance at the match in Ahmedabad brought bad fortune to the Indian team. Gandhi later said, 'PM means Panauti Modi.' The BJP strongly criticized Rahul Gandhi's remarks, describing them as shameful and demanding an apology. Senior BJP leader and former Union minister Ravi Shankar Prasad condemned the comments, calling them disgraceful and linking them to previous Congress criticisms, such as Sonia Gandhi's use of 'maut ka saudagar.' Prasad claimed Rahul Gandhi made these remarks out of frustration over Congress's perceived poor prospects in upcoming elections, warning that BJP would escalate the issue if an apology was not given. India lost to Australia by 6 wickets in the World Cup final at Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, breaking India's 10-match unbeaten run and disappointing millions of fans. After the game, PM Modi met the Indian cricket team, offering encouragement and reiterating the nation's pride in their performance. In a video shared on social media, he was seen consoling captain Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, and embracing bowler Mohammed Shami, praising his efforts.

article_content: Amanda Connelly, Senior Vice President of Leadership Development and Certified Executive Coach at CMP, a minority-women-owned firm, highlights a common challenge in her coaching practice: many executives and emerging leaders are 'voluntold' into people leadership roles without adequate guidance on how to succeed. As a result, these leaders often face steep learning curves, experiencing unnecessary time loss, stress, and challenges, even if they eventually succeed. Organizations that only step in to support leaders once problems arise contribute to higher failure rates among new leaders and create additional stress for their teams. Leadership is not instinctive; it is developed over time through daily interactions, deliberate choices, and reflection. Fortunately, there are strategies to help leaders manage the complexities of their roles. By focusing on the essentials for success, organizations can better prepare employees before they move into leadership positions, whether for the first time or for career advancement. Understanding Scope of Responsibility: New leaders may not fully realize the weight of their responsibilities. Effective leadership requires decisions that impact teams, organizations, and individuals, along with accountability for outcomes. Organizations should help employees understand the breadth of leadership responsibility and encourage development of emotional intelligence and critical thinking skills. Importance of Communication: New leaders sometimes underestimate the role of clear, consistent, and open communication. Poor communication can reduce morale and productivity. Developing strong communication skills—including public speaking, active listening, and nonverbal cues—should be a priority, supported by leaders and mentors. Personal Branding: Every interaction helps shape a leader’s personal brand. The most successful leaders exemplify the strengths they want to see in their teams, including professionalism and alignment with organizational values. Brand development should begin early. Aspiring leaders benefit from guidance to define and build their authentic personal brands throughout their careers. Managing Conflict and Adaptability: Workplaces will always face conflict. New leaders need to see conflict as a chance for growth and innovation when handled constructively. Learning conflict resolution and nurturing an environment of open dialogue, adaptability, and diversity of thought are essential. Effective Delegation: New leaders may try to do everything themselves, but learning to delegate is crucial for effective time management, team development, and achieving goals. Training on team assessment and adapting strategies will help leaders delegate appropriately. Balancing Leadership and Management: Leadership entails vision and inspiration; management covers planning and operations. Success involves both, and new leaders need training to balance them effectively. Organizations should support leaders in developing strategic vision while mastering basic management skills. Conclusion: New leaders face both excitement and challenges. Success requires continual learning, self-awareness, and recognizing the importance of support and development. Understanding the scope of leadership and actively seeking growth set the stage for success. The Forbes Human Resources Council is an invitation-only group for HR executives across industries.

On December 16, 2020, my friend Jade Careaga was found unconscious on a Seattle street. Jade is witty and wise about personal safety—skills she's honed as a trans woman of color involved in sex work. That evening, while planning to meet a client who knew she was trans, a parking mishap led him to cancel their date. Rather than compensating Jade for the damage to her porch, he assaulted her. Sadly, Jade's experience mirrors the harassment and violence that too many trans women face. I'm deeply grateful she's alive and now advocates for survivors of sexual violence.

This is a clear example of what I call the 'desire-to-cruelty' pipeline. Only about four in ten Americans personally know a transgender person, leaving most people to rely on depictions—many sexualized or sensationalized. Alongside a political climate that targets trans healthcare and rights, this often reduces trans people to sex objects, denying them recognition as individuals deserving of love and family life.

Data show trans people are four times more likely than cisgender people to face violent crime. Transphobia is frequently enacted by current or former intimate partners. According to a 2020 Human Rights Campaign report, many violent acts against trans people are committed by men attracted to them. Trans people are 1.7 times more likely to experience intimate partner violence; since 2013, 29% of fatal violence against trans people was by intimate partners.

Media and culture amplify harmful perceptions. In 2022, Pornhub noted a 75% increase in searches for trans porn, with states hostile to trans rights driving many of these searches using derogatory terms. While sex-related media can serve as personal exploration, secrecy in a transphobic context breeds shame. Cisgender men, fearing judgment or questioning of their masculinity, may react with shame or even cruelty toward trans women.

Personally, ex-partners have leaked or threatened to share intimate photos of me without my consent. Men I trusted violated my privacy for profit or out of spite, reinforcing social messages that relationships with trans women undermine masculinity. Feelings of desire coexist with shame and, sometimes, lead to abuse. While 4% of the general population report revenge porn victimization, 15% of LGB individuals do—and the figure is likely higher for trans people.

This cycle of shame often leads to cruelty, rooted in transmisogyny—the notion that masculinity is superior and gender categories are fixed. The U.S. has a history of hypersexualizing women's bodies, especially for those with intersecting marginalized identities like trans women. Examples range from restrictive dress codes to public shaming of women for bodily expression.

The oversexualization and policing of trans women’s bodies are reinforced by sensationalized coverage and offensive stereotypes. Even respected media outlets at times focus excessively on trans bodies or elevate extreme anti-trans positions as normal. These patterns allow politicians to rationalize anti-trans policies, presenting us as threats or political pawns.

Trans people are too often portrayed as dangerous or pitiable, while also being fetishized as 'exotic.' These patterns combine to isolate and endanger our community. Social media misuse and body shaming have forced me to witness the 'desire-to-cruelty' cycle firsthand.

To challenge this, we need authentic trans stories—from trans people themselves—and more representation in everyday, positive roles. As long as discrimination limits our employment and housing opportunities, sex work will be a survival strategy for many. At least 20% of transgender Americans have engaged in sex work, and 72% of trans sex workers report violence. Reporting attacks often leads to the arrest of the worker, not the perpetrator. Decriminalizing sex work and encouraging ethical, consensual trans representation in media are crucial steps. Everyone, especially youth, deserves comprehensive, accurate sexual education, which improves outcomes and reduces stigma.

Ultimately, society must treat trans women—and all trans people—with dignity, respect, and understanding. We should all challenge and unlearn the biases society has taught us about gender and relationships. Together, we can disrupt the 'desire-to-cruelty' pipeline.

article_content: A human-powered helicopter built by University of Maryland engineering students has remained airborne for 50 seconds, beating the team’s previous record of 11 seconds. Called Gamera II, the craft was piloted by engineering student Kyle Gluesenkamp, as shown in a video shared online. The team hopes to win the $250,000 American Helicopter Society Sikorsky Prize for human-powered flight. To qualify, Gamera II must stay in the air for 60 seconds and reach an altitude of three meters. The 50-second flight has not been officially validated yet. Clark School Dean Darryll Pines praised the accomplishment, describing it as an unofficial new world record and highlighting the students’ innovation. Gamera II is closer to the prize criteria than any previous attempt. Its earlier model, Gamera I, first took flight in 2011. Prior to this, student Judy Wexler successfully piloted the helicopter, which is believed to be the first human-powered helicopter flight with a female pilot. Named after a giant flying turtle from Japanese cinema, Gamera is built from lightweight materials and weighs about 140 lbs without a pilot. Each rotor measures 42 feet in diameter, and the craft is 60 feet long, primarily constructed from carbon fiber, foam, and balsa wood. Brandon Bush, a doctoral student and project manager, commented: 'It was beautiful. It jumped up and it stayed there.' Although the National Aeronautic Association must verify the new record, a judge suggested the team has likely set one. Still, the $250,000 Sikorsky Award, created in 1980, remains unwon, as it requires a human-powered helicopter to reach at least three meters and hover for one minute. This achievement marks only the third recorded instance of a human-powered helicopter lifting off. Human-powered helicopter flight is especially difficult because these aircraft lack fixed wings. In 1994, a Japanese team managed a flight lasting 19.46 seconds at a height of eight inches. Dr. Antonio Filippone, from the UK’s University of Manchester, explained: ‘With fixed-wing aircraft, the wings generate lift while propulsion supplies thrust. In a human-powered helicopter, both lift and thrust come from the pilot, meaning far greater force is needed compared to airplanes.’

article_content: GIFT City in Ahmedabad, India, is emerging quickly as a global financial center. According to K Rajaraman, chairman of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), two Japanese banks are joining the community, which currently includes 10 foreign and 16 domestic banks. More than 550 businesses, collectively managing $47 billion in assets, have registered and begun operations in GIFT City. IFSCA serves as the regulator for GIFT City and is working to encourage Indian-origin funds and businesses from overseas tax-free areas to relocate to India. Rajaraman emphasized that GIFT City's streamlined legal and business systems now serve as global standards. A recent IFSCA delegation to Tokyo led to progress with the two Japanese banks, and further interest is being generated through ongoing discussions at the Singapore Fintech Festival in November 2023. At the event, Rajaraman promoted the city’s tax benefits and business advantages. Currently, GIFT City hosts 78 fund managers overseeing 88 alternative investment funds, 82 funds with a combined corpus of $90 billion, five insurance companies, and two stock exchanges: NSE GIFT CITY Nifty and a bullion exchange. The city is also recognized for leasing 122 aircraft through tax-advantaged structures and offers electronic trading platforms for international trade finance, as well as international joint ventures in insurance. In parallel, India’s financial sector is seeing regulatory changes, such as bankers requiring negative liens on personal guarantees for loans to reduce bankruptcy risk. Corporate profits have risen sharply in sectors with a domestic focus. Additionally, gamers are seeking workarounds to access banned real-money gaming apps in states with prohibitions. These trends reinforce GIFT City’s status as a major driver of innovation and financial development in India.

article_content: With holiday travelers filling up flights during peak flu season, it's more important than ever to protect yourself from illness. We investigated major germ hotspots on airplanes and offer key tips to stay safe. While the chances of contracting something severe like meningitis are low, taking precautions is smart.  Germ Zone: Water Airplane water has been under EPA scrutiny after 2004 tests found traces of E. coli, a bacteria that causes stomach cramps and food poisoning. Coffee, tea, or ice may be made with onboard water that isn’t always heated enough to kill all germs. Bottled water can run out, leading crews to fill glasses from the tank—even waiting for sediment to settle. Some aircraft refill tanks at foreign airports with inconsistent water standards. Encouragingly, between 2005 and 2008, only 3.6% of water samples tested positive for coliform bacteria; even fewer had E. coli. In October 2011, stricter EPA regulations (the Aircraft Drinking Water Rule) take effect. Tip: Buy bottled water after passing security. Opt for soda, juice, and prepackaged drinks with no ice to avoid tank water.  Germ Zone: Seat Pocket Seat pockets can harbor cold and flu viruses, along with debris like tissues and wrappers. Viruses survive for hours on fabric and even longer on plastic or metal, so you may pick up more than just magazines. Tip: Use a small carry-on bag instead of the seat pocket, or keep belongings in a plastic bag if you must use it.  Germ Zone: Tray Table Tray tables can be contaminated with MRSA, a serious, sometimes deadly bacterium. A 2007 study found 60% of tray tables from airlines tested positive for MRSA, compared to just 11% on New York subways. Passengers sometimes misuse tray tables, making them a breeding ground for bacteria. Tip: Wipe down your tray table with disinfectant before and after use, and never eat directly from its surface. Protect cuts with bandages, as MRSA is most easily contracted through open skin.  Germ Zone: Airplane Meal Past FDA inspections of large caterers like LSG Sky Chefs found unsanitary conditions and Listeria bacteria, which can cause gastrointestinal illness and, rarely, meningitis. After corrective action, these kitchens passed follow-up inspections. Most travelers face little risk, but caution is wise. Tip: Eat before your flight or bring your own snacks if you're concerned. Hearty sandwiches with cured meats can travel well.  Germ Zone: Airplane Pillows and Blankets Blankets and pillows on planes are often reused with infrequent cleaning. Investigations found bacteria—such as Pseudomonas paucimobilis and Aspergillus niger, which cause lung infections—on these items. In response, some airlines now charge for or no longer offer them. Tip: Dress in layers and bring hand or foot warmers plus your own travel pillow or blanket for warmth and hygiene.  Germ Zone: Lavatory Airplane bathrooms, used by many passengers, are prime spots for germs like E. coli and other bacteria. Bathroom surfaces can spread disease, and flushing can send germs airborne. Even sink water may contain contaminants. Tip: Use a paper towel to close the lid before flushing. Instead of using the onboard sink, use hand sanitizer afterwards for better hygiene.  By being aware and prepared, you can reduce your risk of picking up unwanted germs during your next flight.

article_content: Daniel Noboa, a 35-year-old millionaire heir to a business empire, was sworn in as Ecuador’s new president on Thursday. His inauguration ceremony was attended by Colombian President Gustavo Petro and other foreign representatives. Elected in October on promises to restore peace, Noboa succeeds Guillermo Lasso, who called snap elections amid the threat of impeachment. Noboa will serve the remaining 18 months of Lasso’s term. Ecuador, once peaceful and situated between Colombia and Peru, has recently seen a surge in violence as gangs connected to Mexican and Colombian cartels fight for control. The Ecuadorian Observatory of Organised Crime reports around 3,600 murders linked to drug violence so far this year. This wave of violence affected the election, including the assassination of presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio after a rally. At his inauguration, Noboa acknowledged the challenge ahead, stating, “The task is hard and difficult and the days are few. Let’s get to work.” He emphasized the need to address unemployment and create jobs through urgent reforms to fight violence. Political scientist Santiago Cahuasqui from SEK International University said Noboa, with limited political experience and parliamentary support, will likely preside over a structurally weak government. He stressed the need for a pragmatic and realistic stance to avoid further public frustration. Noboa plans to declare a state of emergency, suspend some civil rights such as freedom of movement, and deploy the military to tackle the drug war. He also suggested offshore prison barges to isolate violent inmates. A wine enthusiast and musician, Noboa was born in Guayaquil to the billionaire banana magnate Alvaro Noboa, who unsuccessfully ran for president five times. Daniel Noboa holds a business degree from New York University and three master’s degrees from Harvard, Northwestern, and George Washington. He started his own events company at 18 before joining the family business. Noboa’s National Democratic Action alliance secured only 17 of 137 seats in October’s parliamentary elections. To form a majority for key appointments, he allied with the leftist movement of former president Rafael Correa and the right-leaning Social Christian Party.

article_content: OXFORD, Mississippi (CNN) — The examination of more than 200 pardons granted by former Mississippi Governor Haley Barbour has raised significant questions about the state’s pardon review process. But none are as perplexing as the case of Harry Bostick. Bostick, a retired Internal Revenue Service investigator, was pardoned by Barbour in January despite being incarcerated in Oxford, Mississippi, for violating his previous DUI sentence—and while he awaited possible charges for a new DUI accident that resulted in the tragic death of 18-year-old Charity Smith. The accident's responsibility has not yet been established. Charity Smith, an aspiring college student from Okolona, Mississippi, lost her life, leaving her mother, Linda Smith, devastated. 'She should still be here with me. This should not have happened,' Linda Smith told CNN in an emotional interview. Bostick received a full pardon for a 2009 felony DUI—his third DUI in just over a year. The Mississippi Parole Board and Barbour both stated they were unaware of Bostick’s arrest in October for another suspected DUI prior to the pardon decision. Oxford Police Sgt. Hildon Sessums had arrested Bostick twice previously for DUI, recounting, 'Right before I put the cuffs on him he said, "Don't do this to me." And my comment to that usually is, you did it to yourself.' For his third DUI, Bostick was sentenced in March 2010 to one year of house arrest and four years in the state’s drug court program, a strict rehabilitation process for convicted felons. He was still involved in this program when he applied for a pardon, supported by letters from friends noting his transformation following personal tragedies—including the loss of his teenage son in a house fire, and a divorce. One letter stated Bostick 'no longer drinks alcohol' and 'has turned his life around.' Retired U.S. attorney Jim Greenlee wrote, 'Harry Bostick has led a tragic life...He can now be a positive factor in many lives.' The Parole Board submitted Bostick’s pardon request to Barbour on September 30, recommending approval by a 3-2 vote. About a week later, on October 7, Bostick was again involved in a suspected DUI crash that killed Charity Smith and severely injured her sister. As of this report, Bostick has not been indicted by a grand jury in connection with the crash. If convicted for the new DUI, because his third DUI was pardoned, this would technically be counted as a third offense—still a felony in Mississippi. The lack of procedures to inform officials about new criminal charges during the pardon process has drawn criticism. State corrections spokespeople referred questions back to the Parole Board, indicating no mechanism is in place for such alerts. Bostick’s application file repeatedly references an 'expedited investigation' into his 2009 crime. According to a prison official, the rush resulted from a surge in pardon applications as Barbour’s term was ending. Governor Barbour declined to be interviewed, but spokesperson Laura Hipp stated, 'In reviewing Mr. Bostick’s case, Gov. Barbour took the Parole Board’s recommendation into consideration, and he wasn’t aware of the subsequent charges.' Parole Board chairwoman Shannon Warnock also said, 'Mr. Bostick’s application was supported by testimonials from trustworthy community members. While the reported circumstances are troubling, everyone is innocent until proven guilty.' Linda Smith fears her daughter’s death is being overlooked in the ongoing controversy. She struggles to comprehend how officials missed the connection between Bostick and the fatal crash involving her daughter. 'She was a person. She wasn’t just some name on a piece of paper. A beautiful person,' said Linda Smith. Now, Linda Smith spends much of her time mourning, often surrounded by her daughter’s artwork. One cherished painting bears Charity’s handprint; another, painted in swirling colors, is inscribed with the words, 'Life is Short.' The young artist whose life showed so much promise is mourned by a mother with a broken heart.

article_content: Ernie Banks, a legendary figure for the Chicago Cubs and a former star of the Negro Leagues, passed away on Friday in Chicago from a heart attack, according to family attorney Mark Bogen. He was just one week shy of his 84th birthday. A public memorial will be scheduled, Bogen confirmed. Cubs Chairman Tom Ricketts called Banks "one of the greatest players of all time" and noted his importance not only to the Cubs and the city of Chicago, but also to Major League Baseball. "He was a pioneer in the major leagues and one of the warmest, most sincere people I've ever known," said Ricketts. Known as 'Mr. Cub,' Banks was admired for his optimistic and kind-hearted nature. Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel described Banks as "one of Chicago's greatest ambassadors," saying that Banks loved the city as much as he loved baseball. On social media, many shared stories and memories of Banks, highlighting his humility, his approachability, and the positive impact he had on those he met. One fan wrote that Banks was "never too big for fans." Banks, despite all his achievements, never won a World Series with the Cubs. The last championship for the Cubs was in 1908. However, Banks remained optimistic and cheerful throughout his career. He became the Cubs' first black player in 1953, after starting his professional career in the Negro Leagues with the Kansas City Monarchs and serving two years in the Army. After joining the Cubs, he quickly made an impact, hitting .314 in 10 games during his first season. He became the starting shortstop the next year, and in 1955 drove in 117 runs, setting a then-record for shortstops with 44 home runs. He later hit 47 home runs in a single season, still a National League record for a shortstop. Throughout his career, Banks was known for his resilience, even after being knocked down by pitchers. He finished his career with 2,583 hits, 11 All-Star selections, two National League MVP awards, and 512 home runs, including five seasons with more than 40 home runs. Banks retired in 1971 and was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1977. He was voted the "Greatest Cub Ever" by fans in 1969. Hall of Fame manager Leo Durocher once said of Banks, "He was one nice guy who finished first – but he had the talent to go with it." Banks was recognized for his generosity and genuine interest in others, often asking people about their families rather than just talking baseball, according to his family attorney. For his contributions on and off the field, Banks received the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, in 2013. At the time, he said, "To have this award passed on to me is certainly a great joy. It's something I'll never forget." President Barack Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama also paid tribute to Banks, recalling his cheerful spirit and the joy he brought to fans across the country. President Obama noted that even as Banks made only $7 a day in the Negro Leagues, he never lost his optimism and love of the game. Ernie Banks' legacy as a sportsman and ambassador will be remembered by many.
